body: Social Security Act 2018 section 65AAA defines accommodation costs for Accommodation Supplement. Owner costs include required mortgage-security payments and reasonably required home payments, excluding service costs and arrears. A resident joint owner's costs are the share MSD is satisfied the person pays. An additional resident in social housing has costs equal to 62% of contributions. A boarder has costs equal to 62% of board and lodging paid. In any other case, costs are rent paid for the premises, excluding service costs and arrears.

Social Security Act 2018 section 65 provides that a person is entitled to an Accommodation Supplement if the person has accommodation costs, meets the assets requirement set out in regulations under section 423, and is not excluded on the social housing exclusion or other funding exclusion grounds.

Social Security Act 2018 section 66 sets the social housing exclusion. A person is ineligible if their accommodation costs include rent for premises let by or on behalf of Kainga Ora, rent for premises let by or on behalf of a registered community housing provider allocated as social housing, or concessionary mortgage-security payments to Kainga Ora or the Crown in right of Te Puni Kokiri.

Social Security Act 2018 section 67 sets other funding exclusions, including a spouse or partner already receiving Accommodation Supplement except as provided in section 68, receiving or being eligible for student allowance basic or independent circumstances grants, specified residential care funding, specified disability accommodation or care funding, and New Zealand superannuation or veteran's pension income above applicable Schedule 5 limits.

Social Security Act 2018 section 68 provides special rules for joint tenants in a relationship. Each couple is treated as one joint tenant, weekly qualifying accommodation costs are the total for both members, and cash assets and income are the total for both members.

Social Security Act 2018 section 69 allows refusal, reduction, or cancellation if available assets have not been realised, includes spouse or partner assets for the assets requirement, requires MSD to refuse a grant if it would be payable at zero, and requires cancellation if granted assistance has been payable at zero for 8 consecutive weeks.

Social Security Act 2018 section 423 authorises regulations for Accommodation Supplement assets requirements, cash-asset exemptions, Area 1 to Area 4 definitions, base rates and assessment of base rates, income-based reductions to the assessed base-rate amount, and rounding. Section 423(3) treats every $100 of cash assets over $5,400 for partnered people and single people with dependent children, and over $2,700 for others, as $1 a week of income for income-based reductions under regulations.

Social Security Act 2018 Schedule 4 Part 7 calculates Accommodation Supplement as 70% of weekly qualifying accommodation costs above 25% of base rate for rent, contributions, or board and lodgings, or above 30% of base rate for homeownership costs, capped by weekly maxima. The maximums are $305, $220, $160, and $120 for partnered people with children or sole parents with 2 or more children in Areas 1 to 4; $235, $155, $105, and $80 for partnered people without children or sole parents with 1 child; and $165, $105, $80, and $70 for other people. Clause 7 defines accommodation income and weekly qualifying accommodation costs as max(0, accommodation costs times 1 minus excluded-area ratio, less accommodation income).

Social Security Regulations 2018 regulation 15 sets the Accommodation Supplement assets requirement. Cash assets must not exceed $16,200 for a person in a relationship or a single person with dependent children, and must not exceed $8,100 in any other case. Applicant assets include spouse or partner assets under Social Security Act 2018 section 69.

Social Security Regulations 2018 regulation 17 defines Accommodation Supplement base rate. It distinguishes beneficiaries and non-beneficiaries, single people and people in relationships, community spouses or partners, dependent-child cases, maximum weekly benefit rates before abatement or deduction, and family tax credit weekly equivalents. This RuleSpec slice treats the assessed base rate as an input pending cross-module wiring to benefit-rate and Working for Families modules.

Social Security Regulations 2018 regulation 18 reduces the Accommodation Supplement amount assessed for a non-beneficiary by 25 cents for every $1 of relevant weekly income above the specified income level. Relevant weekly income is combined applicant and spouse or partner income, except for a community spouse or partner where the applicant's income alone is used. The income level is the amount of income that would prevent payment of Jobseeker Support for the specified family category.
Social Security Regulations 2018 regulation 19 requires every Accommodation Supplement assessed under the Act and regulations to be rounded up to the complete dollar.
